answer.evidence: The pedestal base (rows 36-45, 14 wide) has a light top face over rows 36-41 that steps down to a front-edge line, with a darker front face of about 4 rows (42-45) below it. The lantern roofs (rows 12-17) are sloped planes above an eave line at rows 17-19, and the crossarm (rows 8-10) is a gray band over a dark navy shadow row. The thin post is a vertical shaft joining these parts. No isometric side face is drawn; the object faces south.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, tall prop, but its measured facts sit inside the reference range. It has 14 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge and 17-20 for the stall and well. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no big flat fills. The pedestal top face, gold bands, star finial and the two crowned lanterns with warm glass each show several tone steps (about 4 per material, against 5-6 in the references). Dark edge pixels are 53% near-neutral, so the outline is mixed. Some edges lean toward the material tone, others toward neutral dark. This is not the uniform black sticker line seen on the lamp-crook reference (100% neutral). Texture is modest: the stone pedestal has some grain, and the gold and iron are mostly stepped shading. By eye it is slightly less rich than the well and stall because the post is thin, but it would not look flatter than the reference lamp next to it.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 14 visible tones per full tile, against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The lamp-crook reference, the closest sparse prop, has only 14 raw colours in total, against 25 for the candidate. Judged by eye, the pedestal, gold bands and lit lanterns each carry roughly 3-4 steps with a highlight and a dark side, so the shading is a little shallower than Beodeul's 5-6 but not flat. 53% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is mixed. Some of it is tinted and some is close to black, but it is not a uniform sticker line, and the lamp-crook reference itself measures 100% neutral. At this scale the piece sits comfortably next to the references and does not look thinner or flatter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, sparse prop, so I judged mostly by eye. Facts: 14 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat, 25 distinct colours in total. That is close to the stall (17) and below the well (20), and the lamp-crook reference is also thin. The measured numbers alone don't make it shallow. By eye, though, each material (stone pedestal, iron post, gold bands, crowned lanterns, glass) gets only about 3-4 steps, spread over 25 colours for five materials. The references carry 5-6 steps per material, and the well and stall show per-stone and per-plank texture. The pedestal top and plinth look like smooth stone faces with little per-stone shading or grain. The outline is mixed: 53% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so it leans toward a uniform dark line rather than the dark-material-tone edges the references use. The silhouette is clean and the glass is well lit, but a careful artist would likely see it as slightly thinner and more sticker-like than the references. With the outline mixed and the shading steps below the reference, it fails on the when-in-doubt rule.
